stem:
Esha builds a row of hexagon houses with drinking straws. Shape $1$ uses $6$ straws, Shape $2$ uses $11$ straws, and Shape $3$ uses $16$ straws.

Which countable feature produces the related number sequence $6$, $11$, $16$, $\ldots$?

options.text: Count the straws that make up each whole shape; repeating that same count gives $6$, $11$, $16$, $\ldots$.
Count the straws in Shape $1$ only, then reuse that same count for every later shape.
Count every interior angle from any polygon in the chapter, as if that also made this sequence.
Pick the printed numeral $16$ alone because it is the largest number shown.

teacher.key_rationale: The related sequence is produced by counting the same structural feature—the straws in each whole shape—in every shape. Reusing only Shape 1 omits counting each shape. Stretching the rule to any chapter angle is scope error. Grabbing the printed 16 is surface capture.
